骨格 6 種.name: 6 Skeletons
骨格 6 種.short: How to lay out a page
骨格 6 種.intro:
The **layout** itself for a page. Before deciding which figure to use, decide which of these 6 skeletons to build with.
The default is Skeleton B (figure left + kicker right). Coordinates you can use as-is are in "Skeleton standard coordinates" in [slide-patterns.md](slide-patterns.md).

構成ページ.name: Structural pages
構成ページ.intro: Pages that build the deck's overall framework. `storyline` and `ghost` are both deliverables and design tools used to verify the argument before finalizing the deck.

定量ページ（推移・構成・増減）.name: Quantitative pages (trend, composition, change)
定量ページ（推移・構成・増減）.intro: Pages that make a case with numbers. **All of them require a source line** (`source_note` raises `ValueError` on an empty source). The components reject dual axes and truncated baselines.

比較・評価ページ.name: Comparison / evaluation pages
比較・評価ページ.short: Putting options side by side for a decision
比較・評価ページ.intro: Pages that put options side by side for a decision. For 2 options use a side-by-side layout; for 3 or more use `comparison`; for roughly 3 options × roughly 4 criteria use a rating matrix; when precision matters, use a table.

構造・論理ページ.name: Structure / logic pages
構造・論理ページ.intro: Pages that turn relationships into a diagram. The claim is about **structure**, not numbers.

計画・体制ページ.name: Planning / organization pages
計画・体制ページ.intro: Pages that show time and people — when, who, and what scope.

定性・技術ページ.name: Qualitative / technical pages
定性・技術ページ.intro: Pages that make their case without numbers — quotes, case studies, architecture diagrams, code, and the like.

締め・付録ページ.name: Closing / appendix pages
締め・付録ページ.intro: Pages that handle decisions and what comes after. The principle is to keep the main body thin and the appendix thick.

skeleton-a-full-width.head: Skeleton A | Full-width single figure
skeleton-a-full-width.desc: No kicker; the figure uses the full width. Use this for figures with many elements — such as tables or large trees — that become unreadable when shrunk.

skeleton-b-figure-left-kicker-right.head: Skeleton B | Figure left + kicker right
skeleton-b-figure-left-kicker-right.desc: Places the figure in the left 2/3 and the kicker in the right 1/3. The reader's eye flows figure → kicker, so there's no ambiguity about reading order.

skeleton-c-two-figures.head: Skeleton C | Two figures side by side
skeleton-c-two-figures.desc: Places two figures side by side that support the same claim. If you have two claims, split them across two slides instead.

skeleton-d-two-rows.head: Skeleton D | Two rows, top and bottom
skeleton-d-two-rows.desc: Puts the overall flow in the top row and its breakdown or supplementary detail in the bottom row. Suits wide figures such as processes or timelines.

skeleton-e-full-width-kicker-band.head: Skeleton E | Full-width figure + kicker band below
skeleton-e-full-width-kicker-band.desc: For figures that need full width, such as four-quadrant charts or positioning maps. The kicker sits as a band underneath.

skeleton-f-text-only.head: Skeleton F | Text only
skeleton-f-text-only.desc: For content that needs precision — definitions, premises, conditions — don't force it into a figure. Structure it with a table instead.

exec-summary.head: Executive summary
exec-summary.desc: Opening slide only. Use SCR (Situation → Complication → Resolution) so a decision can be made from this one slide alone. Keep it to at most 5 points.
exec-summary.sample: Make the decision from this one slide

agenda.head: Agenda
agenda.desc: Shows the chapters and page counts up front so readers can grasp the overall scope. If there are many rows, split them by area.
agenda.sample: Show chapters and page counts up front to lower the reader's load

storyline.head: Storyline
storyline.desc: Used as chapter dividers so readers can track where they are. During design, also used to verify the argument.
storyline.sample: Show whether the argument holds up from the titles alone

ghost-deck.head: Ghost deck
ghost-deck.desc: Not a deliverable — a design tool. A checklist to catch "not yet obtained" items before they slip into the final deck.
ghost-deck.sample: Confirm the outline and data sources before finalizing

trend.head: Trend
trend.desc: The basic form for showing change over time. A single axis only (no dual axes). Attach values only at the endpoint.
trend.sample: Operating margin has fallen for three straight years, below the median

waterfall.head: Waterfall breakdown
waterfall.desc: Breaks down the difference between a starting and ending value into contributing factors. The component halts with an error if the total doesn't match the sum.
waterfall.sample: Bridge across the gap to show where the difference came from

composition-pie.head: Composition (pie)
composition-pie.desc: Shows a share of the whole. Up to 6 series. Drawn clockwise in the order passed.
composition-pie.sample: 80% of the reduction potential lies in the reception and reconciliation steps

stacked-trend.head: Stacked trend
stacked-trend.desc: Shows the trend of a total and its breakdown at the same time. If comparing the breakdown components against each other is the main point, use grouped vertical bars instead.
stacked-trend.sample: The total volume is shrinking while staffing costs edge up slightly

grouped-comparison.head: Series comparison
grouped-comparison.desc: Compares 2–3 series within the same category. If you have more than 4 series, switch to a table.
grouped-comparison.sample: The proposed composition cuts effort by more than half in every quarter

kpi.head: KPI
kpi.desc: One or two headline metrics shown large, with breakdowns as horizontal bars. Cramming in too many numbers means none of them stick.
kpi.sample: Narrow down the numbers to take away, and add the breakdown alongside

exhibit-numbered.head: Numbered exhibit
exhibit-numbered.desc: Adding a frame and a number lets you point to it with "see Exhibit 3." Keep it in sync with the exhibit list in the appendix.
exhibit-numbered.sample: A page referenced from the body text and the appendix

two-option-compare.head: Two-option comparison
two-option-compare.desc: Puts the current state and the proposal side by side. This is enough for 2 options — no rating matrix needed.

multi-option-comparison.head: Multi-option comparison
multi-option-comparison.desc: Only add arrows for "transitions." Adding arrows to a parallel comparison implies a left-to-right progression that doesn't actually exist.
multi-option-comparison.sample: Lay out 3+ options side by side and point to a single recommendation

rating-matrix.head: Multiple options × criteria
rating-matrix.desc: Roughly 3 options × roughly 4 criteria is the practical limit. 4-dot ratings work best. For 2 options, a side-by-side layout is enough.
rating-matrix.sample: Dot ratings stay legible even in black-and-white printing

positioning-map.head: Positioning map
positioning-map.desc: Shows relative position along two axes. If you want to show "classification" into four quadrants, use `matrix` instead.
positioning-map.sample: Show position relative to competitors on two axes

balance.head: Balance
balance.desc: Shows the trade-off between two options as weights. Not a quantitative comparison — a figure that shows which way the judgment tips.

spec-table.head: Spec comparison table
spec-table.desc: Lines up numbers and conditions precisely. Keep content as a table when turning it into a figure would lose precision.

logic-tree.head: Logic tree
logic-tree.desc: Breaks a question down with no gaps and no overlaps. A depth greater than 4 is an error. Whether it's truly MECE is the author's responsibility.

pyramid-funnel.head: Hierarchy and narrowing
pyramid-funnel.desc: Places a metric hierarchy (pyramid) alongside a decreasing count (funnel).

layers.head: Layers
layers.desc: Shows a system's responsibilities as layers. The order of the layers itself is the claim.

process-flow.head: Process
process-flow.desc: Shows a process's flow and stages. Use `flow` / `steps` / `icon_flow` depending on the level of granularity.

hub-radial.head: Hub and spokes
hub-radial.desc: A structure where one foundation supports multiple lines of business. Keep the number of spokes to around 6 or fewer.

quadrant-matrix.head: Four quadrants
quadrant-matrix.desc: Positions initiatives on two axes to establish priority. For position relative to competitors, use `posmap` instead.
quadrant-matrix.sample: Position initiatives by impact and cost

venn-iceberg.head: Overlap and depth
venn-iceberg.desc: Combines the overlap of conditions (Venn diagram) with factors that aren't visible on the surface (iceberg).

gantt-schedule.head: Schedule
gantt-schedule.desc: Lays out a process along a timeline. Well suited to explaining a "no downtime" plan such as a phased migration.

roadmap.head: Roadmap
roadmap.desc: Shows a phased path forward. `journey` shows the ups and downs of an experience; `timeline` shows a sequence of points in time.
roadmap.sample: A phased path and a chronological sequence

org-chart.head: Org chart
org-chart.desc: Makes owners and roles explicit. Breaking down a question is `mece_tree`'s job; this one handles the organization.

market-sizing.head: Market sizing
market-sizing.desc: Shows the target scope as nested circles (TAM / SAM / SOM). Pass them from the outside in.

lean-canvas.head: Lean canvas
lean-canvas.desc: Fits the overall picture of a business onto one slide. Don't use it while you still can't fill in every field.

testimonial.head: Testimonial
testimonial.desc: Shows pain points that don't show up in the numbers, through a quote. Works well placed right after a quantitative page.

case-cards.head: Case cards
case-cards.desc: Lays out initiatives as cards so readers can grasp the overall picture. Put individual details in the appendix.
case-cards.sample: Lay out initiatives as cards to convey the overall picture

cloud-architecture.head: System architecture
cloud-architecture.desc: Shows the layout using official cloud icons. **Requires fetching vendor icons** (see above).

code-sample.head: Code sample
code-sample.desc: Trim it down to an amount that's readable on screen. Move long code to the appendix and keep only the key points in the body.
code-sample.sample: Show the specifics of the implementation

pictogram-grid.head: Pictogram grid
pictogram-grid.desc: Organizes business vocabulary with icons. Can be placed at the opening in place of a glossary.

decisions.head: Decisions
decisions.desc: Puts what needs a Yes/No answer onto one slide. Defines the exit point of the meeting right here.

next-steps.head: Next steps
next-steps.desc: Who does what by when. Don't write a line that lacks a subject and a deadline.

appendix-index.head: Appendix
appendix-index.desc: An exhibit index showing where each is referenced from in the body. Keep it in sync with the numbering in `exhibit_frame`.
